name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,795

clue.text: Crook damaged most of table and rug in vehicle

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so its letters are knocked out of order
most, not all, so the last letter of the table goes
the jumbled letters ride inside the vehicle, as passengers do

blocks.note: CAR, the vehicle, opens around the jumble; CA before it
TABL(e) plus RUG, rearranged
the closing R of CAR

explanation.surface: Someone vandalises the furniture and the rug in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints a vandal, which is close to a crook, so the definition hides by blending in.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym at one remove: a cat burglar is a particular kind of thief, one who climbs in through upstairs windows, and every thief is a crook.

clue.text: Vessels moving up Southern Point

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means earlier, so the S climbs one place in the word

blocks.note: cups are drinking vessels
S = Southern: names the letter that moves

explanation.surface: Ships heading north past a southern headland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessels' and 'Point' paint ships rounding a headland; the vessels are crockery, and only one letter shifts.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from geometry and astronomy: a cusp is the sharp point where two curves meet, as at the horns of a crescent moon.

clue.text: Cross about tirade over large adult arthropod

indicators.note: around, so the cross wraps itself about the tirade
in a down answer, what is over sits above, so the cross-and-tirade comes before the rest

blocks.note: a tau cross is T-shaped, named for the Greek letter
rant = tirade, placed inside TA_U
L = large, as on clothing labels
A = adult, an old film certificate

explanation.surface: Someone angrily rants about a huge creepy-crawly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large adult arthropod' reads as one description of the spider; only the last word defines, and 'large adult' supplies L and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: a tarantula is a big hairy spider, and spiders belong to the arthropods, the jointed-legged animals.

clue.text: Taste cut meat maid oddly cut

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are cut away, leaving the even ones

blocks.note: keep the 2nd, 4th, 6th, 8th and 10th letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A maid samples the meat she has sliced.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'cut' looks like a verb about the meat; it is only fodder, and the final 'cut' does the work.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese loanword: umami is the savoury fifth basic taste alongside sweet, sour, salty and bitter, so the definition is its category.

clue.text: Cop recalled self-satisfied male eating donut

indicators.note: called back, and going back means reading backwards
what eats takes the food inside, so the male swallows the O

blocks.note: smug = self-satisfied
he = a male
a donut is ring-shaped, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A smug policeman caught eating a doughnut.
explanation.walkthrough: The cop-and-donut surface is the cliché itself, so the answer sits inside its own picture.
explanation.definitionFit: American slang: a gumshoe is a detective, from the soft rubber soles that let one follow quietly, so a cop in the loose sense.

clue.text: Contractor perhaps also on leave

blocks.note: an ab (abdominal muscle) contracts; 'perhaps' marks it as one example
and = also
used as is

explanation.surface: A builder is also away on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contractor' suggests a builder; here it is a muscle that contracts. 'Leave' reads as a noun, time off, but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym once the part of speech flips: leave as a verb, to go away from and desert, which is what abandon means.

clue.text: Regressive way of paying someone, one crossing a line

indicators.note: regressing is going backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

blocks.note: BACS is the UK's automated bank payment system, used for wages

explanation.surface: A backward way of paying staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regressive' sounds like tax policy, which suits paying people; it is only the turnaround.
explanation.definitionFit: Industrial slang: a scab is a worker who crosses a picket line to keep working during a strike, so the line is a picket line.

clue.text: Musical cabinets not keeping time

indicators.note: the cabinets do not keep hold of the time, so the T is dropped

blocks.note: chests = cabinets, as in a chest of drawers
T = time, removed

explanation.surface: Musical furniture that won't keep time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Musical' looks like an adjective describing the cabinets; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Chess is a 1980s stage musical by Tim Rice and the ABBA songwriters, one musical among many.

clue.text: Painter of note on US phone in Program 1

indicators.note: in a down answer, one thing on another sits above it, so the note comes before the phone
the note and phone sit inside the program and the 1, as a file sits in a folder

blocks.note: a bot is an automated program
ti, the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
Americans say cell for a mobile phone
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A famous artist turns up on a phone app.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of note' reads as 'famous'; split it, and 'note' is its own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: Sandro Botticelli, the Florentine who painted The Birth of Venus, is one painter among many.

clue.text: A long period carrying fruit and feathers

indicators.note: in a down answer, what carries holds its load up on top, so the fruit comes first

blocks.note: a plum is a fruit
'for ages' = for a long period

explanation.surface: Over a long time, a bird carries fruit and grows feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A long period' is one piece, not A plus something; 'ages' is a single idiom for a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym with a number twist: plumage is a bird's whole coat of feathers, and plumages are several such coats.

clue.text: First 365 days hosted by South American country

indicators.note: a host has guests inside the house, so SA holds the year and the one

blocks.note: S = South, A = American
YR = year
first = one = I

explanation.surface: A South American country hosts something for its first year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South American country' looks like one phrase; the definition is only 'country', and it is in the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: Syria is one country among many, on the eastern Mediterranean, nowhere near the South America the surface points at.

clue.text: Counterfeit sale items most spotted

indicators.note: a counterfeit is a false copy, so the letters are rearranged into something that is not what it seems

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: Fake goods at a sale are the ones most often noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' reads as 'noticed'; the definition means covered in spots.
explanation.definitionFit: A literal sense: measly first meant blotched with the spots of measles, so the measliest thing is the most spotted, not the stingiest.

clue.text: One child nursed by Nurse Ruby made better

indicators.note: a nurse cradles a baby in the arms, so RED holds the pair inside it

blocks.note: EN = Enrolled Nurse
ruby is a shade of red; RED opens around the pair
Roman numeral one
CH = child, as in the abbreviation

explanation.surface: A nurse called Ruby looks after a child and makes it better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nurse Ruby' reads as a name; it is two pieces, and only the colour does the nursing.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to enrich something is to improve its quality, as soil or a diet is enriched.

clue.text: Language degrees prior to ChatGPT?

indicators.note: prior means earlier, so the degrees come first in the answer

blocks.note: MAs, Master of Arts degrees
ChatGPT is an example of AI; the question mark flags the example

explanation.surface: Wonders what degrees were worth before ChatGPT.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about technology and education; the answer is an East African language.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: Masai (Maa) is the tongue of the Maasai people of Kenya and Tanzania, one language among many.

clue.text: New pater she finds tiresome at first?

definitions.text: New pater she finds tiresome at first?

indicators.note: something made new is made over, so the letters are reworked into a new order
at the first of each word, so take the initial letters of finds and tiresome

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters
first letters of finds and tiresome, joining the fodder

explanation.surface: A girl finds her mother's new husband a pain.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too, and the question mark admits it: pater is Latin for father.
explanation.definitionFit: An &lit: read straight, the clue describes a new father whom a stepdaughter may resent at the start, which is the stereotype of a stepfather.

clue.text: Shelf further back hides confection

indicators.note: going back means reading from right to left
what hides something keeps it inside, so the letters are concealed in the words

blocks.note: the run starts at the E of shelf and ends at the T of further

explanation.surface: A sweet is hidden at the back of a shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Further back' looks like a place on the shelf; 'further' is fodder and 'back' is the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: a chocolate truffle is a soft ganache ball, one kind of confection or sweet.

clue.text: Bobby still with fellow also going north

indicators.note: north is up the page, so in a down answer the word is read upwards

blocks.note: flat, as in still (not fizzy) water
F = fellow
too = also

explanation.surface: A policeman stays put while a colleague heads north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' reads as an adverb but is the adjective, of drinks without bubbles.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for slang: a bobby is a British police officer, and flatfoot is older American slang for a patrolling cop.

clue.text: Garment extremely ineffective on naked men

indicators.note: at the extremes, so only the first and last letters
stripped of their covering, so the outer letters go
in an across answer, placed after what it sits on

blocks.note: KNIGHTS are chessmen; stripped, they lose their first and last letters
first and last letters of ineffective

explanation.surface: An item of clothing does little to cover naked men.
explanation.walkthrough: Men are chess pieces here, so a solver hunting for a word for 'men' should think of the board.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: a nightie is a nightdress, one garment among many, and apt for the naked men of the surface.

clue.text: Ur art emir reconstructed for 2's home?

indicators.note: rebuilt from the same materials in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: An emir rebuilds the art of ancient Ur.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 is TARANTULA; the question mark marks a definition by example, since a pet tarantula lives in a glass tank.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a terrarium is a glass enclosure for small land animals, and a pet tarantula typically lives in one.

clue.text: Public notice character east of mountain rotated

indicators.note: east is to the right on a map, so in an across answer the character comes after
turned right round, so the mountain is read backwards

blocks.note: an alp is a mountain
a card is an eccentric, amusing person

explanation.surface: A notice about some figure east of a peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' suggests a letter or symbol; it is a person, as in 'he's a real card'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a placard is a notice or sign put up or carried for the public to read.

clue.text: Flower best put below daughter's computer

indicators.note: in a down answer, below means later, so the flower and the best follow the daughter

blocks.note: D = daughter
a flower is something that flows, a river: the Esk, in England and Scotland
top = best

explanation.surface: A daughter's computer is decorated with her finest flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' means a river here: something that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortening: desktop is short for desktop computer, the kind that sits on a desk rather than a lap.

clue.text: Wind and spray facing artist by lake

indicators.note: one thing facing another is set opposite it, so the spray comes first and the artist meets it
by means beside, so the lake goes next

blocks.note: mist = fine spray
RA = Royal Academician
L = lake

explanation.surface: A painter by a lake is caught by wind and spray.
explanation.walkthrough: The seaside painting scene is the disguise; 'Wind' is not general weather but one named wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the mistral is a strong cold northerly wind that blows down the Rhône valley in southern France.

clue.text: Setter accompanying pianist on European mix

indicators.note: keeping company, so side by side and next in line
in a down answer, what is on something sits above it, so the pianist comes before the E

blocks.note: the setter refers to themself as me
Lang Lang, the Chinese concert pianist
E = European

explanation.surface: A crossword setter plays alongside a European pianist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accompanying' sounds musical, suiting the pianist, but only places pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A French loanword: a mélange is a mixture of different things, so a noun mix.

clue.text: Cold place to go in centre of Sleaford

indicators.note: the place to go sits inside the centre letters
the centre of an even-length word is its middle two letters

blocks.note: the middle two of its eight letters
the loo is the toilet, British slang

explanation.surface: Somewhere to go in the middle of Sleaford, a Lincolnshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold' reads like weather for a day out; it describes a manner.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: someone cold in manner is distant and unfriendly, which is what aloof means.

clue.text: Deck game held up with king on board

indicators.note: lifted, and in a down answer lifting means reading upwards
a passenger on board is inside the ship, so the king goes inside the game

blocks.note: polo, the game played on horseback
R = rex, king

explanation.surface: A game is delayed while the king is aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Held up' reads as delayed; it is the turnaround. 'On board' fits the ship picture and the answer is a ship's deck.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautical: the orlop is the lowest deck of a sailing ship, below the waterline.

clue.text: Drinks on small ship, one that pitches

indicators.note: in an across answer, the drinks come after the S

blocks.note: S = small
ales are drinks
to ship a crew is to take them on; to man is to provide the crew

explanation.surface: Drinks on a little boat that rolls about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitches' reads as a ship lurching; it means making a sales pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A pun on pitch: a sales pitch is a persuasive speech, and the one who delivers it to customers is the salesman.

clue.text: Cancel final parts of endless sadistic massage

indicators.note: the final part of a word is its last letter, taken from each of the next two words

blocks.note: the last letters of endless and sadistic
a rub = a massage

explanation.surface: Calling off a cruel, never-ending massage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' tempts you to drop letters; here it is only a word whose last letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal: to scrub a plan or a launch is to call it off, as a scrubbed rocket launch is cancelled.

clue.text: Harmful bugs essentially eroded rocks

indicators.note: the essence, the central letter, is worn away

blocks.note: germs are harmful bugs; its middle R goes

explanation.surface: Harmful microbes have worn down the stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eroded rocks' reads as weathered stone; 'rocks' is slang, as in diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: rocks are jewels, especially diamonds, so gems.

clue.text: Keep info from aged Oscar in shed working

indicators.note: the old man sits in the shed, so those letters go inside HUT

blocks.note: old = aged
O = Oscar in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a hut is a shed, opening around the old Oscar
on = working, as a switched-on machine

explanation.surface: An old man named Oscar is kept in the dark while pottering in his shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aged Oscar' reads as one elderly man; it is two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to hold out on someone is to keep back what you know from them.

clue.text: Rear beams in auditorium

indicators.note: an auditorium is where an audience listens, so the word is heard, not seen

blocks.note: rays are beams of light

explanation.surface: The back beams of a concert hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rear' looks like the noun, the back of the room; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym once read as a verb: to rear a child or animal is to bring it up, which is to raise it.

clue.text: Ready to eat selection of Kashmiri peppers

indicators.note: a selection is a few picked out, here a run of consecutive letters

blocks.note: the run starts at the end of Kashmiri and crosses into peppers

explanation.surface: Kashmiri chillies ready for the table.
explanation.walkthrough: Ripe peppers are the natural reading, so the definition sits in plain sight.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for fruit and vegetables: ripe produce has matured to the point of being ready to eat.

clue.text: 4 and 16 sleeping?

blocks.note: the answers at 4 and 16 down, both slang for police officers
the surface wants officers napping on duty; the setter means lying flat in the road

explanation.surface: Two police officers asleep on duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 4 is GUMSHOE and 16 FLATFOOT, so the clue says 'sleeping policemen', the British name for road humps that slow traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: British idiom: a sleeping policeman is a speed bump, since it slows drivers as an officer would.
